replies:
Here's the first question for your mock interview:

"Tell me about yourself and why this role."

Answer as you would in the room (one to two minutes). I'll score it on structure, evidence and specificity and give one concrete improvement, then ask the next question.

Score (structure, evidence, specificity): 2 / 5.

Why: 
- Structure: your answer is a single sentence describing a technical task, not a brief narrative about you and fit for the role. No opening (who you are), transition to experience, or close tying to the company/role.
- Evidence: it names a method (three-statement model, comps) but gives no example that shows you did it, at what scale, or what result you produced.
- Specificity: vague on inputs and checks (which revenue drivers, what comps, timeline, tools).
One concrete improvement:
- Give a 3-part structure in 30–45 seconds: (1) quick intro: job title + 2 relevant strengths, (2) a short story: one recent example where you built that model (company, size, timeline, tools), and the measurable outcome, (3) why this role: what about the company or team makes you want this role and how you’ll contribute on day one.

Rewritten answer (45–60s) you can practice, fill [brackets] with your details:
"I’m [your title] with [X years] experience in financial modeling and valuation, especially building three-statement models and comps to support M&A and forecasting. At [company], I built a three-statement model from top-line revenue drivers—product mix, churn and new bookings—using Excel and VBA, and used public comps to sanity-check margins; my model shortened our monthly close by two days and supported a pricing change that increased projected annual EBITDA by [Y%/$Z]. I want this financial analyst role because [company’s focus or team], and I’ll start by updating the forecast drivers and delivering a clean, auditable model that the team can use for decision-making."
Next question: ready for a behavioral question? Which one: "Tell me about a time you missed a deadline" or "Walk me through a DCF you built"? (pick one)

You improved from your first reply but I need the exact answer you just gave in the mock to score it honestly. Paste the full version you said aloud (one to two minutes). If you want me to score the rewritten example I provided, say so — otherwise paste yours. One question: do you want the same 3-part rubric (structure, evidence, specificity)?

I’ll prep you: a 10-point plan, the likely question types and 8 practice questions to rehearse (I’ll score your answers if you answer them here). I’ll assume this is a standard final-round interview (60–90 minutes) that mixes technical case or modeling questions, behavioral fit, and deal/industry fit; tell me now if it’s a Superday, partner-only, or timed skills test instead.
10-point prep plan (what to do, in order)
1. Read the posting and any notes you already have about the role so you can match language — I can fetch the posting if you want.
2. Rebuild your top 3 deal stories (one sell-side M&A, one buy-side or advisory support, one analytic/modeling win): for each, state context, your actions (specific models/metrics/techniques), and the impact with numbers.
3. Refresh technical foundations: LBO basics, DCF steps and assumptions, comparable comps selection and multiples, and common accounting adjustments. Have a 1–2 minute verbal walk-through for each.
4. Prepare 3 strong reasons you want Lincoln specifically (firm culture, deal focus, training) tied to concrete evidence (people you met, research).
5. Ready a 30–60s “why you” that links your skills to the analyst job (modeling speed, attention to detail, deal exposure).
6. Prepare answers for common behavioral checks: teamwork conflict, tight deadline, error you found, and a time you improved a process — use STAR with metrics.
7. Prepare intelligent questions to ask partners/interviewers: recent notable deal they led, how analysts are trained/promoted, and what a top-performer did in year 1.
8. Mock a short modeling test: time yourself to build a 3-statement monthly mini-model for 18 months and a simple monthly cash bridge — practice without Excel’s help.
9. Logistics and mental prep: have your resume, deal list, and a one-page cheat sheet (metrics, formulas, negotiation points) ready; plan to arrive early, rested.
10. Closing/offer signals: know your earliest start date, any relocation constraints, and an OK salary range (if they raise it).
Likely question types and how to answer them (short guide)
- Technical: “Walk me through a DCF” — give the steps cleanly: forecast, operating items, FCF to firm/eq, terminal value (exit or Gordon), discount (WACC), sensitivity. Say assumptions and where you’d stress-test them.
- Modeling: “How would you model working capital?” — define the drivers (AR, AP, Inv), express as days or % of revenue, and show how capex, seasonality, or payables terms affect cash.
- Valuation choice: “Why use EV/EBITDA vs P/E?” — EV/EBITDA for capital structure neutral, cross-cap comparisons; P/E affected by capital structure and non-operating items.
- Deal behavior: “Tell me about the most challenging deal you worked on” — focus on your role, the constraint (timeline, data gaps, bidders), action you took, and measurable result.
- Fit/firm: “Why Lincoln?” — connect their mid-market focus, deal types, partner access, or a specific deal you admire to what you want to build.
- Brain-teaser/problem solving: short structured thinking — state assumptions, run a simple model, give a clear recommendation.
8 practice questions (answer any here; I’ll score and give one concrete improvement, then the next)
1. Tell me about a time you drove a financial model under a tight deadline. What did you deliver and what was the outcome?
2. Walk me through a DCF from unlevered free cash flow to enterprise value.
3. Describe a time you found an error in a model or analysis. What did you do and what changed?
4. Lincoln recently advised on [name a mid-market carve-out or deal you saw]; how would you value that business? (If you haven’t seen a specific deal, I’ll give a short case).
5. How do you prioritize tasks when multiple deal deadlines collide? Give a real example.
6. Explain the difference between enterprise value and equity value and a situation where the two diverge materially.
7. Tell me about a time you had to explain complex financial analysis to a non-finance stakeholder. How did you ensure they understood?
8. Do you have any questions for me? (I’ll help you craft 3 tailored questions once you tell me the interviewers’ roles.)

Quick checklist to have on the desk during the interview
- Printed resume + one-page deal bullets with metrics (revenue, EBITDA, multiple, your role).  
- Cheat sheet: common formulas (WACC, terminal value, FCF), comps selection criteria, and 3 questions to ask.  
- Calculator, blank paper, and a pen.
If you want, we can start right now:
- Option A: Practice question 1 — answer as you would in the room and I’ll score it.  
- Option B: I fetch the job posting and a brief on Lincoln’s recent deals to tailor your answers (I’ll need the job link or let me search).

Assuming you want the full, exact field-by-field walk-through for the first posting I prepare, here is exactly what I will fill on the application card and what will be sent to the employer only after you approve it in the extension. I mark anything I cannot fill without something you provide in [brackets].
1) Posting metadata (read-only)
- Company: [as posted]
- Role / Title: [as posted]
- Location: [city / remote / on-site as posted]
- Posting link: [posting URL you gave]
- Posting id: [internal id taken from the posting]
- Pay: [pay text from the posting or "not listed"]
2) Resume to attach
- Which resume file: [I will list available persona names or say "no confirmed resume facts on file"]. Default: use your active persona or "base".
- Resume file name to attach: [filename I will create or a file you uploaded]
- One-line summary of the resume's lead (what the attached resume leads with): e.g., "Leads with: [most recent confirmed role], includes: [degree(s), top skills]."
What I will not do: invent dates, titles, or facts. Any missing facts needed to tailor will be bracketed.
3) Contact/header on resume
- Name: [exact name you tell me to use]
- Email: [exact email you tell me to use]
- Phone: [if you want it included; otherwise left blank]
If you haven't typed name and email in this chat, I'll ask: "What name and email should go at the top of your resume?"
4) Cover note / Message (if posting asks or you request one)
- Addressed to: [hiring manager name if listed, otherwise "Hiring team"]
- Text (<=120 words): three sentences:
1) Opening: state the role and where you saw it. ("I’m applying for [Role] at [Company], posted on [source].")
2) Fit: one sentence connecting a top skill/experience to a key requirement from the posting. ("At [most recent employer], I [what you did] that matches [posting requirement].")
3) Close: availability and prompt to move forward. ("I’m available to start [date or 'immediately'] and welcome the chance to discuss further.")
- Bracketed items where I need your words: [hiring manager name], [where you saw it], [one-line example of your top relevant accomplishment], [earliest start date].
5) Application questions / screening responses
- I will list every required screening question from the posting and propose an answer for each, using only confirmed facts or your explicit words.
- Examples:
- "Are you legally authorized to work in [country]?" → Yes/No (uses confirmed fact)
- "Will you now or in the future require sponsorship?" → Yes/No (uses confirmed fact)
- "Earliest start date?" → [date you provide]
- "Salary expectations?" → I will mirror the posting's format and draft a concise reply; if the posting has no pay listed, I will mark "not listed" and ask your target range.
- Any screening item that depends on personal facts I don't yet have will show as [bracketed question] and I will ask one short question to fill it.

6) Attachments and links
- Files attached: resume PDF (as above), other documents you specify (certificates, transcripts) with exact filenames.
- Portfolio / GitHub / LinkedIn links: included exactly as you provide them. I will not fetch or guess links.
- For each attachment I will show its filename and whether it meets the posting's requested file types.
7) Short free-text answers (if the posting asks for a cover note, elevator pitch, or responses)
- I will draft each required short answer (50–200 words max depending on the field) tailored to the posting's main requirement, with bracketed bits for missing facts.
- Each draft will be concise and show the one metric or outcome the employer wants (e.g., revenue, growth, efficiency, size of team).
8) Checkboxes and Yes/No confirmations
- Items like "Can you travel?" or "Are you willing to relocate?" will be filled Yes/No using only facts you confirmed in prior messages; otherwise they will be bracketed for your answer.
- For "Visa sponsorship required?" the card will show exactly what you told me.

9) Salary / pay fields
- If the posting lists pay, I will copy the posting's pay text exactly.
- If the posting does not list pay and asks for your expectations, I will draft a short answer for you to approve: "[I am seeking $X–$Y base, negotiable]" — I will put your desired range only after you give it.
10) Optional documents / extras
- If an optional portfolio, project summary, or code sample is allowed, I will prepare one short paragraph describing the attached optional file(s) and why it matters to this role.

11) Notes to you (internal)
- 2–3 bullets about fit and gaps taken only from the posting and your confirmed facts. Example: "Strength: 4 years in X; Gap: no explicit cloud cert listed." These are internal and will not be sent to the employer.
12) What will be sent to the employer after you approve the card
- Exact resume PDF file name
- Exact cover note (<=120 words) if requested
- Exact answers to all screening questions (I will show them verbatim)
- Any optional attachments and links you approved

13) What I will not send or do
- I will not submit the application without your approval in the extension.
- I will not invent or confirm facts for you. Any missing personal fact will be bracketed and asked once.
- I will not connect to your email or send messages from your account unless you enable those integrations.
